# Casberi

> Keep it moving, privately. Your life and money are spread across accounts; you spend the day switching apps to get anything done. Casberi is an inbox and a wallet to keep it all moving, privately: keep up with your feeds and finances in one place. Free on iPhone, iPad and Mac, with no Casberi account, and read on your device.

Key facts:

- Free on the App Store for iPhone, iPad and Mac.
- More than 100 apps connect, among them Gmail, iCloud Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Photos, Apple Health, Apple Wallet, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, Notion, Slack, Trello, Stripe, Vercel, Cloudflare, AWS, App Store Connect, Readwise, RSS, Substack, YouTube, Spotify, Bluesky, X, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Telegram, Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Gemini.
- Two places and one act: Feed is what's happening, Wallet is what you have, and Move, the circle at the right, is what you do with your money. Apps, the grid at the top right, holds your apps and Casberi's settings, and its field is Search. On the Mac they run down a rail.
- Feed: every app together, in seven sections — Day, Notes, Social, Work, Media, Life and Agents — each holding today's rows, one row per app. Tap a section for the whole category, or an app for that app alone.
- Wallet: one balance across self-custody accounts (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, World Chain, HyperEVM, Monad, Robinhood Chain, Tempo, Solana and Bitcoin), Coinbase, Kraken, Binance and Gemini, ETH validators, and Wise and Apple Wallet cash. Its pages: Home (your balance, then Account, Needs you, Permissions and Risks), Activity, Holdings and Spending (subscriptions, places, fees and round-ups). Following an account is read-only: you paste an address or a name, never a seed phrase, and it can never move funds.
- Move: an account of your own in three parts — a public account (a Safe on Base, Ethereum and Robinhood Chain, no seed phrase), a private balance (0xBow Privacy Pools and Railgun on Ethereum, picked by the token) and a private account (Aztec, for private apps and payments, proved on the iPhone) — and seven verbs, each approved with Face ID: Buy (with a card, through Stripe), Lend (on Aave), Receive, Send, Spend (on a gift card), Swap and Sweep. Send pays a contact, a name or a zk.money tag. Swaps go straight to Uniswap and Aerodrome from the phone, through Tor; a swap to another network goes through Across. Sweep turns every token under $1 or $5 on a network into ETH in one transaction. On Base, a send short of ETH pays its fee in USDC. Sends can round up to the next $1 or $5: the change earns on Aave and moves into the private balance at $10.
- Apps: a search field over Casberi's settings and every app you have, by category. Contacts (in Social) is everyone you deal with, with Send for a contact who has a wallet and Pay for one with a zk.money tag. Calendar (in Day) opens its own page. The Wallet folder starts with Aztec's directory and the Aztec apps you have connected.
- Subscriptions are found on their own from your cards, Apple Wallet and Rocket Money; what they cost lives in the Wallet's Spending.
- Testnets: the Logos testnet, with test tokens only.
- Agents: read what the agents you use did, in one place. Ask Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and others with your own key, kept in the Keychain and sent from the device straight to that provider; your own OpenAI-compatible server; or Apple Intelligence with no key.
- Notes and voice notes, Contacts across your accounts, and share cards. Widgets for your notes, your wallet and your feed.
- No Casberi account, no server, no analytics. Every request that names a wallet goes through Tor on iPhone and iPad. iCloud sync is opt-in. Export, import and delete-everything are real controls.
